---
title: "Vim — Quick reference"
---

During the computational laboratories you may occasionally need to make a small
change directly on CluMiner: for example, changing a `SHRINK` value, a lattice
parameter, or another CRYSTAL input keyword before submitting a calculation.

For these small edits we use **Vim**, a terminal text editor available on the
cluster. The commands reported on this page are those that will be used the most
for the work required in Mineral Science.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why edit small files directly on CluMiner?

For minor changes, editing the input directly on the Linux cluster avoids an
unnecessary download–edit–upload cycle and reduces possible problems with
Windows line endings.
:::

## The essential idea: Vim has modes

When Vim starts, you are normally in **Normal mode**. In Normal mode, keys are
commands.

To type text, enter **Insert mode**.

To return to Normal mode, press:

```text
Esc
```

::: {.callout-important}
## If you are unsure what Vim is doing

Press `Esc`.

If necessary, press it twice.
:::

## Open a file

```bash
vim mgo_shrink3.d12
```

## Moving around

The arrow keys work and are perfectly acceptable for this course.

Traditional Vim movement keys are:

| Key | Movement |
|---|---|
| `h` | left |
| `j` | down |
| `k` | up |
| `l` | right |
| `0` | beginning of line |
| `$` | end of line |
| `gg` | beginning of file |
| `G` | end of file |

Display line numbers:

```vim
:set number
```

Hide them again:

```vim
:set nonumber
```

## Insert text

Starting from Normal mode:

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `i` | insert before the cursor |
| `a` | insert after the cursor |
| `I` | insert at the beginning of the line |
| `A` | insert at the end of the line |
| `o` | open a new line below |
| `O` | open a new line above |

After editing, press `Esc`.

## Replace text

### Replace one character

Move the cursor onto the character and press:

```text
r
```

followed by the replacement character.

For example, to change:

```text
SHRINK
2 2
```

move to the first `2`, press:

```text
r3
```

and repeat for the second value.

### Replace several characters

Press:

```text
R
```

to enter **Replace mode**.

Type over the existing text, then press `Esc`.

## Delete, copy and paste

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `x` | delete character under cursor |
| `dd` | delete current line |
| `D` | delete from cursor to end of line |
| `yy` | copy current line |
| `p` | paste after current position/line |
| `P` | paste before current position/line |

Duplicate a line with:

```text
yy
p
```

## Undo and redo

Undo:

```text
u
```

Redo:

```text
Ctrl+r
```

## Search for a keyword

In Normal mode:

```vim
/SHRINK
```

then press `Enter`.

Use:

```text
n
```

for the next match and:

```text
N
```

for the previous match.

Other useful searches are:

```vim
/OPTGEOM
/CVOLOPT
/FREQCALC
```

## Replace a word or value

Replace the first occurrence on the current line:

```vim
:s/old/new/
```

Replace every occurrence on the current line:

```vim
:s/old/new/g
```

Replace every occurrence in the file:

```vim
:%s/old/new/g
```

Ask before every replacement:

```vim
:%s/old/new/gc
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not use global replacement blindly

A number or keyword may occur in more places than expected. For changing a
single lattice parameter or `SHRINK` value, direct editing is usually safer.
:::

## Save and quit

Save:

```vim
:w
```

Quit:

```vim
:q
```

Save and quit:

```vim
:wq
```

Quit and discard unsaved changes:

```vim
:q!
```

The two commands worth remembering above all others are:

```text
:wq    save and quit
:q!    abandon changes and quit
```

## A typical course workflow

Create a new input from an existing one:

```bash
cp mgo_shrink2.d12 mgo_shrink3.d12
```

Open it:

```bash
vim mgo_shrink3.d12
```

Inside Vim:

```vim
/SHRINK
```

Change:

```text
2 2
```

to:

```text
3 3
```

then:

```vim
:wq
```

Inspect the result:

```bash
cat mgo_shrink3.d12
```

The same approach can be used to replace placeholders such as:

```text
<X>
<A0>
```

when instructed.

## Check Windows/Linux line endings

Inside Vim:

```vim
:set fileformat?
```

A normal Linux file should report:

```text
fileformat=unix
```

If it reports:

```text
fileformat=dos
```

convert it with:

```vim
:set fileformat=unix
:w
```

## Show invisible characters

```vim
:set list
```

Return to the normal view with:

```vim
:set nolist
```

## Jump to a line number

For example:

```vim
:40
```

moves to line 40.

## Built-in help

```vim
:help
```

Useful examples:

```vim
:help substitute
:help :write
```

Exit help with:

```vim
:q
```

## Interactive tutorial

From the Linux shell:

```bash
vimtutor
```

## Minimal command set to remember

| Command | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Esc` | return to Normal mode |
| `i` | insert text |
| `r` | replace one character |
| `R` | Replace mode |
| `/text` | search |
| `n` | next search result |
| `u` | undo |
| `:w` | save |
| `:wq` | save and quit |
| `:q!` | quit without saving |
